issue.acceptance_test: A reader who sees only the figure can state that attention (and K/V production) happens once per layer, not once per token.

issue.issue: Type inside the boxes is cramped and appears below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor: the Attention box's sub-label 'compute Q,K,V for this vs all past tokens' wraps to two lines that nearly fill the box, and the sub-labels throughout ('user prompt', 'characters', 'BPE splits', 'corpus-driven', 'ordered integers', 'ID to d-dim vector', 'one vec/token', 'read + write per layer + head') are set noticeably smaller than the box titles.
issue.evidence: In the 150 dpi render (580 px for 8.5 in = 68 px/in) the sub-label glyph height is ~4-5 px, i.e. roughly 6-7 pt at print size, versus ~8-9 px (~11-12 pt) for the box titles. The Attention box (x~255-340, y~340-380) contains two lines of sub-label with ~3 px clearance top and bottom.
issue.root_cause: Boxes were sized to fit the diagram rather than the type, and the annotation type size was not checked against the book's figure-annotation floor.
issue.correction: Enlarge the sub-label type to the figure-annotation floor (>= 8 pt at print size) and widen/heighten the affected boxes (Attention, KV Cache, Embedding) to accommodate it without wrapping into the box border; shorten the strings if necessary ('compute Q,K,V (this + past)').
issue.acceptance_test: At 100% print size on US Letter, every figure annotation is >= 8 pt and no text touches a box border.

issue.issue: The caption refers to 'the backward arrow from the KV cache back to attention', but that arrow is drawn as a routed return path below the boxes, not as a backward arrow; and the caption's 'Color is figure-local decoration' disclaimer is not carried by Figs. 1.1 and 2.1, which also rely on color to distinguish read from write and to identify the initialize path.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'the KV cache is a persistent state — written (append) and read (attend, the backward arrow from the KV cache back to attention) across steps — not a processing stage.' In the figure the green 'read past K,V' arrow leaves the bottom of the KV Cache box, runs left below the Attention box, and turns up into the Attention box's bottom edge. Figs. 1.1 and 2.1 have no color disclaimer.
issue.root_cause: Caption written against an earlier draft of the layout; the disclaimer was added to one caption only.
issue.correction: Describe the arrow by its label ('the green/grey arrow labelled read past K,V') rather than by direction, and add the same color disclaimer to Figs. 1.1 and 2.1 (or make the palette global and drop the disclaimer everywhere).
issue.acceptance_test: Every caption's description of an arrow matches the arrow's drawn geometry and label, and the color convention is stated wherever color carries meaning.

issue.issue: Sub-annotation type in the token column ('sampled from prefill', 'first decode output', 'second decode output', 'adds one K/V') and in the stored-K/V boxes ('layer L . h1-hn') appears to fall below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor, and the last token box's sub-label ('adds one K/V') is an action rather than a provenance, unlike the other three.
issue.evidence: Rendered sub-label glyph height ~4-5 px at 68 px/in, i.e. ~6-7 pt at print size, versus ~8-9 px for the bold box titles. The four token boxes carry three provenance labels and one action label.
issue.root_cause: Annotation type size was not verified against the book's stated floor; the token column was filled with whatever text fit.
issue.correction: Raise sub-annotation type to >= 8 pt at print size (widening the token column if needed) and make the fourth box's sub-label parallel in kind ('nth decode output' or 'adds one K/V at step n+1').
issue.acceptance_test: All figure annotations measure >= 8 pt at print size; the four token sub-labels are grammatically parallel.

issue.issue: In the conclusions list beneath the figure, the capacity item's unit reads as '~1.19 FLOPS/FLOP demand', which is not a unit; the intended quantity is presumably ~1.19x10^15 FLOP/s. If the exponent is genuinely absent, the comparison to the 989 TFLOPS H100 peak does not parse.
issue.evidence: Printed p.23, item (2): 'the stated TTT deadline implies ~1.19 FLOPS/FLOP demand, exceeding the compared single-H100 theoretical peak (989 TFLOPS)'. The comparison is only meaningful if the demand is 1.19x10^15 FLOP/s (which does exceed 9.89x10^14).
issue.root_cause: Possible lost superscript or a genuine unit typo in a summary list that was not re-read against the derivation.
issue.correction: Verify the source and print '~1.19x10^15 FLOP/s' (or the correct value) with the exponent intact; if the demand is in fact 1.19 FLOP/s, the conclusion is wrong and must be rewritten.
issue.acceptance_test: The unit in item (2) is a rate (FLOP/s) with a legible exponent, and the stated inequality against 989 TFLOPS is arithmetically true of the printed number.

issue.figure: FIGURE 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue.issue: The MoE expert grid shades FOUR of the eight cells with the 'active' orange fill (E1, E4, E5, E6), while the panel label reads 'top-2 active' and the legend defines the orange swatch as 'active experts = 2'. A reader scanning the figure infers that 4/8 experts (50% of expert weights) are touched per token, instead of 2/8 (25%). This is the single most consequential number in the figure and the drawing contradicts its own label and legend.
issue.evidence: Rendered right-hand grid, row by row: E1 (orange), E2 (gray), E3 (gray) / E4 (orange), E5 (orange), E6 (orange) / E7 (gray), E8 (gray) — four orange cells. Red label above the grid: 'top-2 active'. Legend line beneath: 'active experts = 2 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. Caption: 'the two routed experts (~11.4B + ~5.7B)'. Orange-cell count (4) vs 'top-2' (2) vs legend '2' — three-way inconsistency inside one figure.
issue.acceptance_test: Re-render at print size and confirm exactly two cells carry the active fill (e.g. E1 and E5) with the other six gray. If four cells are intentional (e.g. the union of active experts across two tokens), add an explicit legend entry distinguishing 'active for this token' from 'active for another token' and state the token count in the caption. Acceptance: orange-cell count equals the number stated in the 'top-2 active' label and in the legend.

issue.issue: The caption's active-per-token decomposition does not sum to its own stated total and disagrees with the total drawn inside the figure. The caption conflates the routed-only figure (22.8 GB) with the routed-plus-shared figure (25.6 GB) and mis-states the per-expert split.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'only ~22.8 GB is active per token: the always-on attention/shared weights (~1.4B) plus the two routed experts (~11.4B + ~5.7B)'. 1.4B + 11.4B + 5.7B = 18.5B params → 37.0 GB at 2 bytes/param, not 22.8 GB. Figure line: 'active per token: 11.4B top-2 = 1.4B per token = 12.8B → 25.6 GB always-on' (12.8B → 25.6 GB). Legend: 'inactive experts = 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' implies each expert is 11.4 GB = 5.7B params, so two routed experts = 11.4B params = 22.8 GB, and 8 × 5.7B + 1.4B = 47.0B → 94 GB, matching the caption's '~94 GB'. The caption's '(~11.4B + ~5.7B)' should be '(~5.7B + ~5.7B)' and its '22.8 GB' should be '25.6 GB' if the shared weights are included.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption sentence so the decomposition sums: '~22.8 GB of routed expert weights is active per token (2 × 5.7B); adding the always-on attention/shared weights (~1.4B) gives ~25.6 GB of weights touched per token, against ~94 GB resident.' Verify: 1.4 + 5.7 + 5.7 = 12.8B → 25.6 GB; 8 × 5.7B + 1.4B = 47.0B → 94 GB; 68 + 22.8 + 2.8 = 93.6 GB ≈ 94 GB.

issue.issue: The legend label for the active experts appears to read '2 GB resident' while its own parenthetical '(2 × 11.4)' and the caption both give 22.8 GB. If the label literally reads '2 GB', the resident total in the figure collapses to 72.8 GB and contradicts the caption's '~94 GB'.
issue.evidence: Rendered legend line: 'active experts = 2 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. 2 × 11.4 = 22.8 GB. Caption: '~22.8 GB is active per token' and '~94 GB' resident. Cross-check: 68 GB (inactive) + 22.8 GB (active) + 2.8 GB (shared 1.4B) = 93.6 GB ≈ 94 GB, which only closes with 22.8, not 2.
issue.acceptance_test: Inspect the source string for this legend entry; it must read '22.8 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'. If it currently reads '2 GB', correct it and re-verify that the three legend quantities (68 + 22.8 + 2.8) still sum to ~94 GB.

issue.issue: The figure's active-per-token line uses '=' where the intended relation is addition, producing a false equation on the page.
issue.evidence: Drawn text: 'active per token: 11.4B top-2 = 1.4B per token = 12.8B → 25.6 GB always-on'. Read literally this asserts 11.4B = 1.4B. The intended chain is 11.4B (routed) + 1.4B (shared) = 12.8B → 25.6 GB.
issue.acceptance_test: Change the two '=' between the parameter counts to '+' (or '→') so the line reads '11.4B top-2 + 1.4B shared = 12.8B → 25.6 GB always-on'; confirm 12.8B × 2 bytes = 25.6 GB.

issue.figure: FIGURE 3.4 — KV comparison boxes ('dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB')
issue.issue: The KV comparison is not reproducible from the shape labels printed beside it. A reader who recomputes from '32L/4096H GQA' gets a 5× ratio, not the 20× that the drawn totals imply, so the figure invites a false inference about how much of the KV saving comes from GQA versus from layer count.
issue.evidence: Drawn: 'dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB' with '8-bit KV set by shape, not routing: 80L/8192H MHA vs 32L/4096H GQA'. Dense: 2 × 80 × 8192 × 1 B = 1.31 MB/token → 12.05 GB at 9,200 tokens (consistent with the house 8-bit KV figure of ~1.31 MB/token). MoE from the printed shape: 2 × 32 × 4096 × 1 B = 0.262 MB/token → 2.41 GB at 9,200 tokens, i.e. 5× dense, not 0.6 GB. 0.6 GB is reachable only with 8 KV heads × 128 head-dim (2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 1 B = 0.0655 MB/token → 0.60 GB), a fact the figure never states.
issue.acceptance_test: Add the KV-head count and head dimension to the shape label (e.g. '32L/4096H, 8 KV heads × 128') and state the context length both totals assume (9,200 tokens), so that 12 GB / 0.6 GB = 20× is derivable from the printed text; otherwise recompute and redraw the two totals. While editing, confirm the italic sub-label is at or above the 8 pt print floor and that the legend text is not smaller than the 8 pt floor.

issue.figure: FIGURE 6.1 — The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain
issue.issue: The two vertical arrows appear to point opposite to the directions stated by the caption and by the figure's own inline key. As rendered, the left arrow labelled 'causation' carries its arrowhead at the TOP (next to 'Workload metrics') and the right arrow labelled 'diagnosis' carries its arrowhead at the BOTTOM (next to 'Serving metrics') — i.e. the drawn directions invert the stated causal chain. This is the chapter's central mental model (workload → resource → serving) and the figure is the only place it is drawn.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'Causation runs downward (workload → resource demand → serving behavior); diagnosis runs upward (serving symptom → resource evidence → workload/context).' Inline key under the boxes: 'causation ↓ (workload → resource → serving) | diagnosis ↑ (serving → resource → workload)'. Rendered arrowheads: left vertical line at the 'causation' label terminates in a head at the top edge of the 'Workload metrics' box; right vertical line at the 'diagnosis' label terminates in a head at the bottom edge of the 'Serving metrics' box. The drawn arrows therefore contradict both the caption and the inline key.
issue.acceptance_test: Inspect the source at print resolution and confirm arrowhead placement: the 'causation' arrow must point DOWN (Workload → Resource → Serving) and the 'diagnosis' arrow must point UP (Serving → Resource → Workload). If the heads are as rendered, swap the arrowheads (or swap the two labels) and re-render. Acceptance: drawn arrow directions, inline key, and caption all agree.

issue.figure: FIGURE 3.2 — Dependency order and cache lifetime, panel B
issue.issue: The caption claims out-of-order acceptance, but the diagram shows strictly in-order, left-to-right acceptance. The distinction between 'full-canvas masked sampler' and 'block-causal sampler' is exactly the point of the figure, and the drawing does not exhibit it.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'a full-canvas masked sampler: accepts positions out of order while recomputing bidirectional states'. Panel B draws: fixed prompt → [? ? ? ?] → [A B C ?] → [A B C D]. Every accepted ID appears in its final left-to-right position, and the dashed recompute region always covers the rightmost unresolved cells. No panel shows an ID accepted at a later position before an earlier one, so 'out of order' is asserted in prose but not depicted.
issue.acceptance_test: Either redraw panel B so at least one accepted ID appears out of position (e.g. [? B ? ?] → [A B C D], with the dashed recompute region covering the whole canvas), or amend the caption to 'accepts selected IDs while recomputing bidirectional states' and add a note that the drawing shows one in-order acceptance order for illustration. Acceptance: the caption's ordering claim is either visible in the drawing or explicitly scoped.

issue.issue: The figure's legend vocabulary refers to a 'solid bracket' element that the drawing does not contain, and the one mark that could play that role appears in only one panel. A reader cannot tell which visual element encodes 'finalized prefix state'.
issue.evidence: Note under panel A: 'Solid brackets mark finalized prefix state, not just accepted IDs.' Caption: 'Solid brackets identify finalized prefix state'. The drawing contains only per-cell boxes (all solid) plus dashed orange recompute rectangles; no bracket element distinguishes finalized from non-finalized state, and the trailing '-' cell in panel A's last group is drawn identically to the finalized 'A B C' cells. A short underline appears beneath the trailing cell of panel A's third group only, and is explained nowhere. The dashed outline IS explained ('Dashed outline = recomputed output region'), so the unexplained element is specifically the 'solid bracket'.
issue.acceptance_test: Add an explicit legend (or one caption sentence) naming every visual element — cell box, dashed recompute rectangle, underline — and state which one marks finalized prefix state; apply the finalized-state mark consistently in panels A, B, and C, or delete the underline and remove the 'solid brackets' wording from both the note and the caption.

issue.figure: FIGURE 3.1 — panel B, masked discrete diffusion
issue.issue: In the masked-diffusion lane the sequence GROWS from three tokens to four across the corruption step, which implies that masking changes sequence length. For a book whose later chapters reason about per-token KV growth and context-length arithmetic, a figure that shows length changing under corruption is a substantive mis-teaching.
issue.evidence: Panel B: left state shows three cells 'A | cat | sat'; the corrupted state shows four cells 'A | M | sat | M'; the fully masked state shows four cells 'M | M | M | M'. The left box is also visibly narrower than the other two. A corruption process q must preserve length; the caption calls the panel 'a categorical-MASK lane' and notes 'text states are illustrative token IDs, not generated results'.
issue.acceptance_test: Make all three states the same length (e.g. 'A | cat | sat | sat' → 'A | M | sat | M' → 'M | M | M | M', or 'A | cat | sat' → 'A | M | sat' → 'M | M | M') and keep the three boxes the same width; re-check that the 'M = MASK' note still explains every cell.

issue.issue: Panel A labels its three states; panel B does not, so the reader must map the three boxes by position alone and infer which is clean, which is corrupted, and which is fully masked.
issue.evidence: Panel A carries 'clean diffusion data', 'partly corrupted', 'noise prior' beneath the three boxes. Panel B's three boxes have no labels; the only key is the note 'M = MASK; text states are illustrative token IDs, not generated results.'
issue.acceptance_test: Add the same three state labels under panel B's boxes, or restructure the figure with one shared label row serving both lanes, so the two lanes are read identically.

issue.issue: The 'noise prior' state is drawn as a structured histogram rather than an uninformative one, so the visual contrast between structured data and isotropic noise is absent and the reader can infer that the prior retains the data's structure.
issue.evidence: Panel A, right box labelled 'noise prior', shows bars of clearly unequal heights (a tall bar at the left, shorter bars elsewhere) whose profile closely resembles the 'clean diffusion data' panel. The caption calls the drawing 'Conceptual drawing, not a measurement', which does not license a structurally misleading profile.
issue.acceptance_test: Draw the noise-prior panel with a flat or near-uniform bar profile (or annotate it '≈ uniform / uninformative') so the contrast with the structured clean-data panel is unambiguous; retain the 'not a measurement' caveat.

issue.issue: This caption is set in italic and appears centred, while every other caption in the batch is roman and justified. A single figure breaking the caption convention reads as a production accident.
issue.evidence: Printed p.91: 'FIGURE 6.1: The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain [ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]. The three tiers layer the bottom-up diagnostic path...' is fully italic, including the figure number, and the lines are centred. Compare FIG 3.1 (p.31), FIG 3.2 (p.33), FIG 3.3 (p.43), FIG 3.4 (p.47), FIG 4.1 (p.72), FIG 5.1 (p.88) — all roman, justified, same size and leading.
issue.acceptance_test: Match the caption environment used by the other figures (roman, same size/leading, justified rather than centred) and re-render; confirm the caption block is visually indistinguishable in style from FIG 5.1 on the facing chapter.

issue.figure: FIGURE 5.1 — Model selection for RAG workload
issue.issue: The word 'quality' appears both as one of the five selection surfaces and, in the caption, as an evaluation gate, so the figure's bullet can be read as the very thing the caption says is excluded from the figure.
issue.evidence: Figure box: 'Five selection surfaces / quality · latency · KV cache · S/tok · retrieve-vs-generate'. Caption: 'they are deliberately distinct from the end-to-end evaluation gates (retrieval quality, reranking, embedding recall, and final answer quality) that a RAG system must also pass'.
issue.acceptance_test: Rename the bullet to 'model quality' (or 'output quality') so it cannot be conflated with the caption's evaluation gates, keeping the caption's distinction intact.

issue.figure: FIGURE 5.1 — box fills and grayscale behavior
issue.issue: Green is reused for two semantically different boxes, and the four fill colors are close in luminance, so the figure's hierarchy weakens in grayscale and the green reuse invites the reader to group 'Workload characterization' with the 'Generation leg'.
issue.evidence: 'Workload characterization' (top box) and 'Generation leg' are both green; 'Five selection surfaces' is pink, 'Retrieval leg' purple, 'RAG system decision' blue-gray. At 150 dpi grayscale the green and pink fills are nearly the same lightness, and no shape or weight distinguishes the boxes.
issue.acceptance_test: Assign a distinct fill (or a distinct border/label treatment) to each of the five boxes, or introduce a shape/weight distinction that survives grayscale; verify the figure remains readable when converted to grayscale at print size.

issue.figure: FIGURE 3.3 — Wan2.2 A14B: active ≠ resident parameters
issue.issue: The horizontal connector between the two stage boxes is drawn as a plain data-flow arrow and can be read as the high-noise stage's output feeding the low-noise stage, rather than as temporal progression of the denoising schedule. Its label also duplicates the arrowhead with a trailing '→' glyph.
issue.evidence: A solid horizontal arrow runs from the 'High-noise stage' box into the 'Low-noise stage' box, with the text 'Denoising schedule progresses →' centred above it. The temporal meaning is carried only by the label and by the figure's note 'Not two experts within one forward' and the caption's 'as the denoising schedule progresses'; the connector itself has the same visual grammar as the data-flow arrows elsewhere in the book.
issue.acceptance_test: Change the connector to a clearly temporal form (a dashed timeline arrow, or a 'then' label without the trailing '→' glyph), or add a small 'time →' marker, so the reader cannot read the connector as tensor flow.

issue.figure: FIGURE 4.1 — Six-dimension workload characterization mapped to architectural decisions
issue.issue: The figure draws exactly one arrow per dimension, which visually asserts the one-to-one mapping that the caption explicitly disclaims. A reader who skims the figure (and skips the caption) will carry away a deterministic mapping model.
issue.evidence: Six blue dimension boxes each connect by a single dashed arrow to one tan decision box (e.g. 'Latency SLO' → 'TTFT/TPOT & batch window'). Caption: 'The arrows are non-exclusive: in practice a dimension often influences several decisions at once (e.g. Latency SLO shapes both model choice and serving configuration), and the six axes are a starting lens, not a partition.'
issue.acceptance_test: Add one or two secondary arrows (e.g. Latency SLO → model size / type) or a footnote marker on the arrow set stating 'primary influence shown; other couplings exist', so the drawing does not contradict the caption.

issue.issue: The '1 · FACT' box contains an unexplained token '099' between 'baseline TTFT' and '450 ms'. It reads as a stray number or a broken figure cross-reference (the prose on printed p. 390 points the reader at 'Fig 26.1' for the workload), and a reader cannot tell whether '099' is a value, a figure id, or a rendering artifact.
issue.evidence: Rendered box text: 'baseline TTFT 099 450 ms'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'the architect reads the capstone's workload against Fig 26.1 — short prompt, latency-sensitive, moderate quality'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'These components sum to a ~450 ms baseline TTFT budget'. No quantity named '099' exists anywhere in the visible prose.
issue.acceptance_test: The box reads 'baseline TTFT (Fig 26.1) 450 ms' or 'baseline TTFT 450 ms' with no unexplained token; the printed value still equals the prose's ~450 ms baseline TTFT budget; re-render at 150 dpi and confirm no stray glyphs remain.

issue.issue: The figure asserts as 'FACT' exactly the three quantities the prose explicitly says are NOT facts. Box 1 is headed '1 · FACT' and contains 'request rate ~2 rps', 'utilization 45%', and the baseline TTFT — the same three values the prose labels as assumed scenario inputs that 'become FACTS only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test'. Figure and prose therefore assign different evidence classes to the same numbers, which is the book's central provenance discipline.
issue.evidence: Figure box 1: '1 · FACT / request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT … 450 ms'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTS (R-07): no author-run load test produced them, so they are labeled an assumed baseline for a worked example (an input to the math), not a measured runtime quantity a FACT would be. They become FACTS only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test.'
issue.acceptance_test: Either relabel box 1 with the book's own assumption/scenario label from the Ch. 4 taxonomy (e.g. '1 · ASSUMED BASELINE (scenario input)'), or change the prose so the capstone values are presented as instrumented facts. The figure's evidence label and the prose's evidence class for the same three numbers must be identical, and the caption must state which it is.

issue.issue: The caption describes the loop as 'closing on FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN', which omits the return arrow to FACT — the only element that makes this a feedback loop rather than a three-step pipeline. The figure's own subtitle calls it the 'Pattern-Measurement-Feedback Loop', so the caption understates the drawn structure.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'FIGURE 26.2: Pattern Application Diagram: the Pattern-Measurement-Feedback Loop applied to the capstone scenario, closing on FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN.' Drawn arrows: 'trace' (FACT→DERIVED), 'validate' (DERIVED→PATTERN), 'feedback' (PATTERN→FACT).
issue.acceptance_test: Caption reads '…closing the loop FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN → FACT', naming the return edge explicitly.

issue.issue: The return path carries two labels with unclear ownership: 'feedback' on the vertical leg and 'adjust + pick pattern' on the horizontal leg leaving the PATTERN box. A reader can reasonably read 'adjust + pick pattern' as the label of the PATTERN→FACT arrow (i.e. the loop's action) or as a separate step, and the two readings imply different control flow.
issue.evidence: Rendered: red horizontal segment from the PATTERN box's left edge labelled 'adjust + pick pattern'; red vertical segment rising to the FACT box labelled 'feedback'.
issue.acceptance_test: One label per arrow, or an explicit ordering: the PATTERN→FACT arrow carries a single label (e.g. 'feedback: adjust + pick pattern') and the intermediate segment carries no competing text.

issue.issue: Box 2 states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as an unqualified DERIVED result, while the prose treats the regime as conditional on batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware. The figure is the more quotable artifact, so an unqualified label risks becoming the universal claim the book elsewhere avoids.
issue.evidence: Figure box 2: '2 · DERIVED / decode bandwidth-bound'. Prose, printed p. 390: 'sharding distributes the model across the node so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8, batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there)'.
issue.acceptance_test: Box 2 reads 'decode bandwidth-bound (baseline regime; see Ch. 8)' or carries a short qualifier, matching the prose's conditionality.

issue.issue: The metric scope is stated only for the GLM row ('BF16 / layer', 'attention only per head / layer'). The two DeepSeek rows carry no scope annotation, so the reader cannot tell what the denominator of '100% → 7%' and '100% → 10%' is (total KV cache across all layers and heads? per-token? per-layer?). The footnote's '*Metric scopes differ' flags the problem without resolving it, and the caption's 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope' implies but never states the DeepSeek scope.
issue.evidence: Figure rows: 'DeepSeek V4-Flash … KV cache* 100%→7% / Compute* 100%→10%' (no scope note) vs 'GLM-5.3-Flash … 100%→23% (BF16 / layer) / 100%→33% (attention only per head / layer)'. Footnote: '*Metric scopes differ. 7% remaining = 93% reduction.' Caption: 'GLM's rows are per-layer/per-head scope, not total FLOPs or total cache'.
issue.acceptance_test: Every row states its scope inline (e.g. 'DeepSeek: total KV cache, all layers' / 'total attention FLOPs'), or the figure carries a scope column; the caption's scope sentence covers all three rows, not only GLM.

issue.issue: The caption contains a broken sentence: 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (…) and under-provisioning.' The clause 'and under-provisioning' is ungrammatical and the intended consequence (that the architect under-provisions) is left unstated.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (using a model whose vendor reports 7% KV vs 1M context as if it were 100%) and under-provisioning.'
issue.acceptance_test: Sentence reads, e.g., 'An architect who re-derives them per candidate model would then re-derive the model-specific KV and FLOP constants (using a model whose vendor reports 7% KV vs 1M context as if it were 100%) and would under-provision.'

issue.issue: The caption runs to roughly 200 words across two paragraphs, mixing figure description, provenance rules, a cross-reference to Fig 7.1, a teaching-model statement, and a worked misreading. A caption this long is read as body text and is unlikely to be read at all; the parts that are not caption material should move into the surrounding prose.
issue.evidence: Caption begins 'FIGURE A.1: Vendor-relative KV/compute ratios.' and continues through '…not yet independently reproduced on a serving stack (see A.2).'
issue.acceptance_test: Caption is reduced to what the figure shows (rows, scope, the not-a-ranking caveat, sources); the 'same message as Fig 7.1's CQOA line' and the 'architect who re-derives them' worked misreading move to adjacent body text with a forward reference from the caption.

issue.issue: The smallest annotations ('reported 2026-06', 'reported 2026-08', 'BF16 / layer', 'attention only per head / layer', and the two-line source footnote) render noticeably smaller than the rest of the figure and are at risk of falling below the book's 8 pt print floor. These are not decorative: the dates and the scope notes carry the figure's provenance argument.
issue.evidence: Rendered at 150 dpi: the gray 'reported 2026-06' / 'reported 2026-08' lines and the italic footnote are visibly smaller than the row labels and column headers.
issue.acceptance_test: Print proof at 100% shows every annotation in FIG A.1 at ≥8 pt, including the footnote and scope notes; if any is smaller, raise it or move the content into the caption.

issue.issue: Red is used for two unrelated meanings inside one figure: the 'NOT A CROSS-MODEL PERFORMANCE RANKING' warning callout and the DeepSeek V4-Flash row identity (row label and its two arrows). A reader can associate the warning with that row, or read the row as 'the flagged one'.
issue.evidence: Red-bordered red-text callout 'NOT A CROSS-MODEL PERFORMANCE RANKING'; row label 'DeepSeek V4-Flash' in red with red arrows '100%→7%' and '100%→10%'; the other two rows use blue and green.
issue.acceptance_test: The warning callout uses a neutral treatment (black/gray border and text) or a distinct non-row hue, so no row identity color is reused for a caveat; row identity colors remain consistent across the appendix.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue.issue: The legend promises a shade encoding that the figure does not implement: 'darker shade = MoE transition ~2022'. All three efficiency-led bands (Transformer ~2017, Efficient Transformer ~2020, MoE Transformer ~2022) are drawn in the same brown, so the legend's only within-family cue is inert, and the reader cannot locate the 'MoE transition' the legend points at. The legend also shows only one brown swatch, so the ramp is never demonstrated.
issue.evidence: Legend: 'Efficiency-led (dashed) — context / cost / capacity; darker shade = MoE transition ~2022' with a single brown swatch. Bands: 'Transformer ~2017', 'Efficient Transformer ~2020', 'MoE Transformer ~2022' all rendered in the same tan/brown fill.
issue.acceptance_test: The MoE Transformer band is rendered in a visibly darker brown than the two bands above it and the legend shows both shades (or the 'darker shade' clause is deleted); the distinction survives a grayscale conversion.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue.issue: The caption ends with a dangling clause: 'a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era overlap.' The second conjunct has no predicate, so the sentence does not parse. The intended point (that the era markers overlap, so the layering is not a strict succession) is left unstated.
issue.evidence: Caption: '…the vertical stacking is a layering (which capabilities sit on which substrate), not a causal lineage: a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era overlap. Read it as "what exists at each stage" not "what caused what".'
issue.acceptance_test: Caption reads, e.g., '…a later layer does not require the one below it, and the era markers overlap.' — a complete sentence with a predicate.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue.issue: The base 'Transformer ~2017' band is drawn in the efficiency-led (brown, dashed) family, but the base transformer is not an efficiency-led layer; the legend's category label therefore misclassifies the bottom band. The reader is told the brown family means 'context / cost / capacity' and then finds the origin of the stack in it.
issue.evidence: Legend: 'Efficiency-led (dashed) — context / cost / capacity'. Bands: 'Transformer ~2017' (brown, dashed), 'Efficient Transformer ~2020' (brown, dashed), 'MoE Transformer ~2022' (brown, dashed).
issue.acceptance_test: Either the base Transformer band is given its own legend category (e.g. 'Foundation (solid)') or the legend's brown family is renamed to cover it (e.g. 'Model architecture (dashed) — foundation, efficiency, MoE'), so no band contradicts its legend entry.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue.issue: Evidence-label scope mismatch between the figure and its caption: the in-figure subtitle closes with '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', while the caption labels the figure only '[ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual'. The figure therefore claims a derived component that the caption does not acknowledge, leaving the reader unsure which span the DERIVED label binds to.
issue.evidence: In-figure subtitle: 'Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive chronology; approximate era markers (≈), not release dates. [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'. Caption: '…Read it as "what exists at each stage" not "what caused what". [ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual'.
issue.acceptance_test: The figure's internal label and the caption's label agree, or the caption explicitly splits the span (e.g. '[ILLUSTRATIVE] band structure; [DERIVED] era markers') so the DERIVED label has a stated referent.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.2 — A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems
issue.issue: The legend's first two entries are distinguished primarily by hue (brown vs blue) with border style as the only redundant cue; in grayscale the brown and blue swatches are close in luminance, so a grayscale reader must decode the legend by border style alone. The third entry (purple, thick) is separable, but the family boundary between 'efficiency-led' and 'capability-led' is not.
issue.evidence: Legend swatches: brown with dashed border, blue with solid border, purple with thick border; the bands repeat the same three treatments.
issue.acceptance_test: Grayscale conversion of the figure still lets a reader assign every band to a legend family without relying on hue (e.g. add a hatch or a left-edge marker to one family, or separate the families with a rule).

issue.figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue.issue: The figure's central semantic distinction — 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs' — is carried by hue alone. In grayscale the four blue bands and three green bands collapse into two overlapping luminance ramps, and the boundary between 'Inside test-time search' (blue, system) and 'Inside post-training' (green, model) becomes unreadable. That boundary is the figure's whole point.
issue.evidence: In-figure note: 'blue = where the system runs · green = where the model runs'. Bands: 'Across a fleet of models', 'Inside agent runtime', 'Inside tools', 'Inside test-time search' (blue family); 'Inside post-training', 'Inside MoE routing', 'Inside attention', 'Inside weights' (green family).
issue.acceptance_test: A grayscale rendering of FIG A.3 still shows which side of the system/model boundary each band falls on — e.g. a horizontal rule plus a group label ('system-side' / 'model-side') at the boundary, or a hatch on one family; the hue note remains as a secondary cue.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue.issue: The figure draws a large upward red arrow labelled 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights', which encodes a directional, upward-is-more-advanced reading, while both the in-figure note and the caption insist the axis is 'not a ranking'. The drawn arrow is the strongest visual element on the page and it contradicts the stated semantics; a reader is likely to conclude 'up is better'.
issue.evidence: In-figure note: 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights (vertical axis = WHERE it lives: nonexclusive placement choices, not a ranking)'. Caption: 'The horizontal bands are a design choice (which layer owns which capability), not a ranking of superiority; a lower band is not "better" or "worse" than a higher one'. Rendered: a single-headed red arrow rising from the 'Inside weights' band to the 'Across a fleet of models' band.
issue.acceptance_test: The arrow is either made double-headed with a label that names it as an observed trend rather than a preference (e.g. 'observed direction of travel, not a recommendation'), or removed and replaced by a neutral axis marker; the caption's 'not a ranking' claim and the drawn geometry must be mutually consistent.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue.issue: Chapter references inside the figure use two different formats — a range with an en dash ('Ch 17–20') and a comma list ('Ch 19, Ch 24') — within the same right-hand column, and the range form is used only once. The reader cannot tell whether the difference is meaningful.
issue.evidence: Right-hand labels: 'Ch 18, Ch 20'; 'Ch 17–20, Ch 24'; 'Ch 19, Ch 24'; 'Ch 8, Ch 20'; 'Ch 19, Ch 21'; 'Ch 10'; 'Ch 7, Ch 8'; 'Ch 3, Ch 8'.
issue.acceptance_test: One format is used throughout the figure (e.g. 'Ch 17, Ch 18, Ch 19, Ch 20, Ch 24'), and the same format is used in the book's other figure-embedded chapter references.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.3 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue.issue: The arrow's explanatory text is set in small red type, centered under the band stack and detached from the arrow it describes, while the arrow itself carries no label. The reader's eye enters at the arrow (the only saturated element) and finds no text attached to it.
issue.evidence: Rendered: a red vertical arrow at the far left with no adjacent label; the red note 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights (vertical axis = WHERE it lives: nonexclusive placement choices, not a ranking)' sits below the bands, centered, in small type.
issue.acceptance_test: The arrow carries its label adjacent to the shaft (rotated or in a short callout), and the note is set at the same size as the other in-figure annotations.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue.issue: In the 'Exit after pass 2' row, the solid orange arrow to the 'exit' box originates from the dashed 'pass 3' box that is explicitly labelled 'not executed'. The drawn geometry therefore shows the exit occurring after pass 3's slot, directly contradicting the row heading 'Exit after pass 2' and the caption's 'A true exit omits later work'. A reader can infer that the exit happens after pass 3 — the opposite of the figure's point.
issue.evidence: Rendered row 1: 'pass 1 → pass 2 → [pass 3, dashed, 'not executed'] → exit', with a solid orange arrow from the dashed pass-3 box to the orange 'exit' box. Row heading: 'Exit after pass 2: two different runtime paths'. Caption: 'A true exit omits later work; selecting an earlier representation after all passes does not.'
issue.acceptance_test: The exit arrow originates from 'pass 2' (the last executed pass), or the pass-3→exit connector is drawn dashed and the exit box is labelled 'exit (after pass 2)'; no solid flow arrow may leave a box marked 'not executed'.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue.issue: In the upper diagram, the 'one shared core weight set' box appears to connect by dashed weight-reuse arrows to pass 1 and pass 3 only; no dashed arrow to pass 2 is visible. If pass 2 lacks the weight-reuse arrow, the diagram contradicts its own title ('Shared-depth execution reuses weights') and the legend ('Dashed arrows = weight reuse'), implying that the middle pass does not use the shared weights.
issue.evidence: Rendered upper diagram: dashed vertical arrows visible from the weight-set box down to 'pass 1' and to 'pass 3'; the segment above 'pass 2' is not distinguishable at 150 dpi. Legend: 'Dashed arrows = weight reuse; dashed box = not executed.'
issue.acceptance_test: Verify at print size that all three passes receive a dashed weight-reuse arrow from the shared weight set (or that the omission is explicitly explained); if the middle arrow is missing, add it.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue.issue: The two lower runtime-path rows omit the shared weight set entirely, so the reader cannot see that the exit and selection paths still execute against the same shared weights — the very distinction the figure's title draws ('reuses weights, not necessarily history state'). The lower rows also drop the history-cache boxes, so the 'not necessarily history state' half of the claim is untested in the part of the figure that shows the interesting paths.
issue.evidence: Rendered: upper diagram contains 'one shared core weight set' plus three 'iteration N history cache' boxes; the 'Exit after pass 2' rows contain only pass boxes and the exit/selection boxes.
issue.acceptance_test: The lower rows either repeat the shared weight set (with dashed reuse arrows) and the per-iteration caches, or carry a one-line note stating that the shared weights and caches are omitted for clarity and are unchanged from the upper diagram.

issue.figure: FIGURE A.4 — Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state
issue.issue: The smallest in-figure text — the 'not executed' annotation under the dashed pass-3 box and the two-line legend ('Dashed arrows = weight reuse; dashed box = not executed. Solid arrows = flow; labeled boxes mark exit / selection. Illustrative exit index; no latency or quality result.') — is set below the size of the other annotations and is at risk of falling under the 8 pt print floor. The 'not executed' label is load-bearing for the figure's central claim.
issue.evidence: Rendered at 150 dpi: 'not executed' and the legend block are visibly smaller than the box labels ('pass 1', 'exit', 'select pass 2 after pass 3').
issue.acceptance_test: Print proof at 100% shows 'not executed' and the legend at ≥8 pt; if not, enlarge them or move the legend into the caption.

issue.figure: FIGURES 26.2, A.1, A.2, A.3, A.4 (book-level pattern)
issue.issue: A systematic pattern: each of these figures prints a title inside the figure and then repeats it verbatim as the caption's opening words ('Pattern Application Diagram', 'A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems', 'Where should intelligence live?', 'Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state'). The caption therefore adds no information at the point where the reader needs it, and the reader's eye is asked to read the same sentence twice.
issue.evidence: FIG 26.2 in-figure title 'Pattern Application Diagram' = caption opening; FIG A.2 in-figure title 'A conceptual layering of frontier AI systems' = caption opening; FIG A.3 in-figure title 'Where Should Intelligence Live?' = caption opening; FIG A.4 in-figure heading 'Shared-depth execution reuses weights, not necessarily history state' = caption opening.
issue.acceptance_test: For each figure, either the in-figure title is dropped (caption carries the title) or the caption opens with what the figure shows rather than restating the title; no figure's caption begins with a verbatim copy of its in-figure title.

issue.figure: FIGURE 7.5 (KV cache size vs context, by attention geometry)
issue.issue: The caption's 'Scope:' sentence is internally incoherent and contradicts the figure's own legend and annotations. As rendered it reads (fragments): 'Scope: FP16 is 2.62 MB/token, FP8 is half that, ~1.31 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget) at 128K for the FP16 full-MHA footprint is ~535 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget); the GQA FP8 footprint, ~24.9 GB at 9.5K (total tokens with KV residency) — then ~16 GB (vs the ~436 GB budget).' Each of the four numeric claims fails against the figure's own encoding.
issue.evidence: Recomputation from the legend values (2.62 MB/tok full-MHA FP16; 0.33 MB/tok GQA FP8): (a) 'FP8 is half that, ~1.31 GB' — the per-token FP8 value is ~1.31 MB/token (also stated in the figure's own note above the legend: '~1.31 MB/token'); 'GB' is a 1000x unit error. (b) 'the GQA FP8 footprint, ~24.9 GB at 9.5K' — 9,500 x 0.33 MB = 3.1 GB, which is exactly what the figure's own annotation says ('9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)'); 24.9 GB is the full-MHA FP16 value (9,500 x 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB), i.e. the caption attributes the full-MHA number to the GQA curve. (c) 'at 128K ... ~535 GB' — 128,000 x 2.62 MB = 335 GB; the drawn full-MHA FP16 marker at x=128 sits BELOW the 436 GB budget line, consistent with 335 GB and inconsistent with 535 GB. (d) 'then ~16 GB' — GQA FP8 at 128K = 128,000 x 0.33 MB = 42 GB; 16 GB corresponds to no quantity in the figure. The sentence also contains three parenthetical '(vs the ~436 GB budget)' insertions and a run-on with no grammatical subject, indicating an editing failure rather than a single typo.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the 'Scope:' sentence so that every number is (i) recomputed from the legend's per-token values, (ii) consistent with the two in-plot annotations ('9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)', '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)'), and (iii) consistent with the drawn marker positions at x=128. Specifically: FP8 = ~1.31 MB/token; full-MHA FP16 at 9.5K = 24.9 GB and at 128K = ~335 GB (below the 436 GB budget); GQA FP8 at 9.5K = 3.1 GB and at 128K = ~42 GB. Then re-render and confirm the caption contains no number that is not derivable from the legend.

issue.issue: The caption states 'GQA with a 64:1 query:to-KV head ratio is 8x lower'. A 64:1 query-to-KV ratio is MQA and would reduce KV by 64x, not 8x. The book's own geometry (FIG 7.1, printed p. 108: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)' = 64 query heads, 8 KV heads) is 64:8, which is what produces the 8x saving shown in the figure and the '8x saving (Ch. 7)' annotation.
issue.evidence: FIG 7.1 annotation: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)'. FIG 7.5 legend: full-MHA FP16 ~2.62 MB/tok vs GQA FP16 ~0.66 MB/tok (4x) and GQA FP8 ~0.33 MB/tok (8x). The 8x figure is consistent with 64:8, not 64:1. The caption as rendered therefore states a head ratio that contradicts both the figure it captions and the preceding figure in the same chapter.
issue.acceptance_test: Confirm the ratio string in the source. If it reads '64:1', change to '64:8' (or '8:1 per group'); if it reads '64:8', no change. In either case, add a one-clause cross-reference to FIG 7.1 so the 8x factor is traceable to the head geometry rather than asserted.

issue.issue: The caption contains a duplicated clause and a lowercase sentence start, both visible in the rendered page: 'The full-MHA FP16 curve is the conservative upper-bound baseline; GQA with a 64:1 query:to-KV head ratio is 8x smaller; full-MHA does the conservative upper-bound baseline.' and 'GQA, FP8/8-bit). parameter count does not determine KV size'.
issue.evidence: The clause 'full-MHA does the conservative upper-bound baseline' restates the first clause of the same sentence. The sentence beginning 'parameter count does not determine KV size' follows a full stop and a closing parenthesis but begins with a lowercase 'p'. Both are visible on the rendered page (printed p. 123, caption lines 2 and 4-5).
issue.acceptance_test: Delete the duplicated clause and capitalize 'Parameter'. Re-render and confirm the caption reads as a sequence of complete, non-redundant sentences.

issue.issue: The two horizontal reference lines in the legend — '8xH100 (raw, 640 GB)' and 'KV budget ~436 GB' — are separated by only 0.17 decades on a 4-decade logarithmic y-axis (log10(640)=2.81, log10(436)=2.64). At print size they are effectively coincident, and neither line is labelled in place, so a reader cannot tell which dashed line is which or where the full-MHA FP16 curve crosses the budget.
issue.evidence: Plot y-axis spans 0.1 to 1000 GB (4 decades). The two reference values differ by 640/436 = 1.47x, i.e. 0.17 decades = ~4% of the axis height. In the 150 dpi render the two dashed lines are within a few pixels of each other; the legend is the only disambiguator, and the legend entries are themselves distinguished only by dash colour (grey vs blue), which is a colour-only distinction that degrades in grayscale.
issue.acceptance_test: At 100% print size, confirm the two reference lines are individually traceable. If not: label each line in place (e.g. '8xH100 = 640 GB' at the right end of the line, 'KV budget ~436 GB' likewise), and/or replace the 640 GB line with a single annotated line, and/or add an explicit marker where the full-MHA FP16 curve crosses the 436 GB budget (~166K tokens). Ensure the two lines differ by more than dash pattern alone.

issue.issue: The in-plot annotation '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)' is ambiguous: the figure plots two GQA curves (GQA FP8 ~0.33 MB/tok and GQA FP16 ~0.66 MB/tok), and 3.1 GB corresponds only to the GQA FP8 curve (9,500 x 0.33 MB = 3.1 GB; GQA FP16 would be 6.2 GB). A reader can reasonably attach the label to the wrong curve.
issue.evidence: Legend lists 'GQA FP8 (~0.33 MB/tok)' and 'GQA FP16 (~0.66 MB/tok)' as separate series; the annotation names only 'GQA'. The companion annotation '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' is unambiguous because only one full-MHA FP16 curve exists.
issue.acceptance_test: Relabel to '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA FP8)' and confirm the leader line terminates on the GQA FP8 marker.

issue.issue: The annotation '8x saving (Ch. 7)' has no visible anchor or leader line, so the reader cannot determine which pair of curves it compares (full-MHA FP16 vs GQA FP8, or full-MHA FP16 vs GQA FP16, which is only 4x).
issue.evidence: The other two in-plot annotations ('9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)', '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)') carry leader lines to their markers; '8x saving (Ch. 7)' is free-floating text in the upper-right of the plot area.
issue.acceptance_test: Add a leader line or a bracket/arrow spanning the full-MHA FP16 and GQA FP8 curves at a stated context length, and state the pair explicitly ('8x saving: full-MHA FP16 vs GQA FP8').

issue.issue: The note enumerating the full-fine-tune memory components does not sum to the plotted bar value of ~1,120 GB. As rendered it reads 'Full-tune: FP16 weights + FP16 grads + Adam m/v (2 x 16 B/param).' The listed components either give 2+2+32 = 36 B/param (2,520 GB) or, if the parenthetical is '2 x 4 B/param', 2+2+8 = 12 B/param (840 GB). Neither equals the plotted 1,120 GB.
issue.evidence: 1,120 GB / 70e9 params = 16 B/param exactly. The only standard mixed-precision Adam configuration that yields 16 B/param is FP16 weights (2) + FP16 grads (2) + FP32 master weights (4) + FP32 Adam m (4) + FP32 Adam v (4) = 16 B/param -> 1,120 GB. The FP32 master-weight copy is not visible in the note as rendered, so the figure's own derivation does not close.
issue.acceptance_test: Verify the source string for the note. If the FP32 master copy is absent, add it and state the total explicitly ('16 B/param -> 1,120 GB'); if the parenthetical reads '2 x 16 B/param', correct it to '2 x 4 B/param'. Acceptance: the note's components sum to the plotted bar value, and the sum is shown.

issue.issue: The first note appears to have an unbalanced parenthesis: 'Each bar is a conditional floor (weights + the listed states, not a full deployment config.' with no closing parenthesis before the period.
issue.evidence: Visible on the rendered page (printed p. 124, first note line). The same note block otherwise uses balanced parentheses ('(2 x 16 B/param)', '(Table 7-2)').
issue.acceptance_test: Check the source string and close the parenthesis (or restructure the sentence). Re-render and confirm punctuation balance across all five note lines.

issue.issue: The 'Inference (weights+KV)' bar (~165 GB) visibly crosses the '2xH100 (160 GB)' reference line, but the figure annotates only the QLoRA bar ('QLoRA fits a single H100') and the full-fine-tune bar ('Full fine-tune exceeds an 8xH100 host: needs multi-node or offload'). The most operationally important crossing in the figure — inference does not fit on 2x H100 — is left for the reader to infer.
issue.evidence: Bar top ~165 GB vs the 2xH100 dashed line at 160 GB; the crossing is visible in the render but unlabelled, while the other two bars each carry an interpretive annotation.
issue.acceptance_test: Add an annotation on the inference bar stating the implication (e.g. 'Inference exceeds 2xH100 (160 GB) at 9.5K context') so all three bars carry the same interpretive treatment.

issue.issue: The KV term in the inference bar is not attributed to an attention geometry. The bar's ~165 GB = 140 GB FP16 weights + ~24.9 GB KV, and 24.9 GB is the full-MHA FP16 bound at 9.5K (per FIG 7.5). A reader who has just absorbed FIG 7.1 and FIG 7.5 may assume the canonical model uses GQA and compute 140 + 6.2 = 146 GB, contradicting the bar.
issue.evidence: FIG 7.5 annotation '9.5K = 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' (full-MHA) vs '9.5K = 3.1 GB (GQA)' (GQA FP8); FIG 7.6's caption says only 'weights + KV' with no geometry qualifier.
issue.acceptance_test: State the geometry in the figure or caption, e.g. 'Inference (weights + full-MHA FP16 KV at 9.5K)', and cross-reference FIG 7.5 so the 24.9 GB term is traceable.

issue.issue: The shaded 'SLO-violating' region does not begin at the SLO line. The caption states 'the light band marks the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line', but the drawn light-pink band starts at approximately 4.4 s, well to the right of the 2 s SLO line, leaving the interval (2 s, ~4.4 s) unshaded.
issue.evidence: In the render, the blue dash-dot SLO line is at x = 2 s and the pink band begins near x = 4.4 s; the darker hatched sub-band covers the ~5 s straggler cluster. The caption's parenthetical '(> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line' describes a band that starts at 2 s. A reader can therefore infer that no request violates the SLO between 2 s and 4.4 s, which is false as a statement about the region (it is empty of data, not empty of violations).
issue.acceptance_test: Either extend the light band to start at the 2 s SLO line, or change the caption to 'the light band marks the straggler cluster region (~4.4-6 s), all of which lies beyond the 2 s SLO line'. Acceptance: the drawn band and the caption describe the same interval.

issue.issue: The annotation box reports 'p99 = 1.33 s' with no qualifier, but 1.33 s is the p99 of the finite N = 10,000 sample, not of the stated workload. The prose on the facing page (printed p. 92) is explicit that 'the population p99 of the stated 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mix is 5.0 s' and that the sample p99 'still looks healthy'. The figure alone licenses the wrong inference the section exists to correct.
issue.evidence: Printed p. 92: 'p99 ~ 1.33 s - a knife-edge property of this N = 10,000 sample, not of the distribution ... the population p99 of the stated 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mix is 5.0 s'. Figure annotation: 'mean = 0.85 s / p99 = 1.33 s / (p99 still looks fine)'. The caption's 'p50/p90/p95/p99 read off the stream' is not carried into the annotation itself.
issue.acceptance_test: Relabel the annotation to 'sample p99 (N = 10,000) = 1.33 s' and add 'population p99 = 5.0 s' as a second line, so the figure carries the section's actual lesson rather than the trap. Acceptance: a reader who sees only the figure cannot conclude that the workload's p99 is 1.33 s.

issue.issue: The figure plots 'Request latency (s)' and draws an 'SLO 2 s' line, but the prose identifies the same 2 s budget as the canonical p95 TTFT SLO ('Under the canonical p95 TTFT SLO of <= 2 s ...'). TTFT and end-to-end request latency are different quantities (request latency >= TTFT always), so the figure applies a TTFT budget to a request-latency distribution.
issue.evidence: Printed p. 92: 'Under the canonical p95 TTFT SLO of <= 2 s, even this sample's p99 (~ 1.33 s) still looks healthy'; and later on the same page 'We budget TTFT <= 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s) with a p95 <= 2 s.' FIG 6.2's x-axis is 'Request latency (s)' and its caption is 'Request-latency distribution'.
issue.acceptance_test: Decide which quantity the 2 s SLO governs and make the figure and the prose agree: either relabel the axis/line as TTFT, or relabel the line 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget applied to request latency)' and add one clause in the prose noting that request latency is bounded below by TTFT. Acceptance: no page in Ch. 6 uses 'SLO 2 s' for two different metrics.

issue.issue: The p90 (0.94 s) and p95 (0.99 s) reference lines are separated by 0.05 s on a 0-6 s axis, i.e. ~0.8% of the plot width (~2-3 px at 150 dpi). The two green dashed lines are effectively coincident, so the reader cannot verify the p90/p95 values the prose quotes from the figure.
issue.evidence: Prose on printed p. 92 quotes 'p50 ~ 0.80 s, p90 ~ 0.94 s, p95 ~ 0.99 s, and p99 ~ 1.33 s' as read off the plotted histogram. On the rendered page the p90 and p95 lines overlap; only their stacked labels at the top-left distinguish them.
issue.acceptance_test: Add a zoomed inset over the 0.7-1.4 s region, or annotate the percentile values numerically at each line, so p90 and p95 are separately readable at print size.

issue.issue: Two wording defects in the figure's own text: (a) the caption contains a stray unmatched closing parenthesis — 'the light band marks the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s); everything right of the SLO line) and the darker hatched band ...'; (b) the in-plot annotation '1% stragglers (>5 s cross the SLO)' misdescribes the cluster, which is centred at 5 s and spans roughly 4.4-6 s, so only its upper half is '> 5 s'.
issue.evidence: Both strings are legible on the rendered page (printed p. 93). The caption's parenthetical is opened at '(> 2 s)' and closed, then a second ')' appears after 'SLO line' with no matching '('.
issue.acceptance_test: Remove the stray ')' and change the annotation to '1% stragglers (all beyond the 2 s SLO)' or '1% stragglers (~5 s, all beyond the 2 s SLO)'. Acceptance: caption punctuation balances and the annotation's inequality matches the drawn cluster.

issue.issue: The outer container box is titled 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)', yet the note inside the same box reads 'Container wraps tensors + metadata: e.g., GGUF / safetensors'. The box therefore conflates the checkpoint file format (the container) with the packed tensor payload (its content), and the inner box ('Layout, padding and alignment are implementation-specific') has no title of its own. The reader cannot tell which box is the file and which is the payload.
issue.evidence: Rendered structure: large rounded rectangle whose bold heading is 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)', containing a smaller titled box 'Layout, padding and alignment are implementation-specific' and the note 'Container wraps tensors + metadata: e.g., GGUF / safetensors'. The caption refers to 'packed tensors and checkpoint container' as two distinct things, which the drawing does not show.
issue.acceptance_test: Retitle the outer box 'Checkpoint container (e.g., GGUF / safetensors)' and move 'Packed tensors: values + scales (+ zero points, if used)' to the inner box heading. Acceptance: the drawing shows two distinct, correctly named levels matching the caption's vocabulary.

issue.issue: The three bottom boxes ('Native FP4 math', 'Fused dequant', 'Reconstruct') are mutually exclusive execution paths, but the connector from 'Runtime tensors in the kernel-required layout' fans into them without any 'one of' marker, so the diagram can be read as a sequential pipeline.

The caption's 'Unsupported combinations may be rejected' reinforces the alternatives reading but is not in the drawing.

issue.issue: The figure's own legend states 'Arrows = token input / state flow', but no arrow is drawn from the 'token t1 / t2 / t3' labels into the 'recurrent update' boxes; the only arrows are the horizontal state-flow arrows between update boxes and the vertical arrows from update boxes to state snapshots. issue.issue: The figure's note 'Recurrent updates compute; state and KV boxes store' introduces a compute-vs-storage distinction that the visual language does not carry consistently with the rest of the chapter: KV/state storage is orange in FIG 7.1, red/pink in FIG 7.2, and uncolored gray in FIGS 7.3-7.4.
issue.evidence: FIG 7.1 (printed p. 108): K/V boxes are orange with white 'K/V' text. FIG 7.2 (printed p. 110): state boxes are red-bordered/pink, KV boxes are red-bordered. FIG 7.3 (printed p. 114) and FIG 7.4 (printed p. 116): all boxes/bars are neutral gray. No chapter-level legend maps color to compute vs storage.

Acceptance: the same concept carries the same visual treatment across the chapter's figures.

issue.issue: The subtitle asserts 'Payload and local-scale bar widths are proportional to bytes', but the two 1-byte NVFP4 scale segments are drawn at roughly half the width of the 1-byte MXFP4 scale segment, so within-bar proportionality does not hold.
issue.evidence: In the render, the MXFP4 row's single dark segment (1 B scale) is about twice the width of each of the NVFP4 row's two dark segments (2 B scales total). The payload segments are consistent (~21 px/B in both rows), so the discrepancy is confined to the scale segments, which are drawn at a minimum visible width rather than proportionally.
