issue.issue: The caption instructs the reader to 'Read the two bars', but the figure is a three-curve line chart with no bars; the caption also refers to 'this two-line calculation' two sentences later, so the caption contradicts itself about the figure's geometry.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'Reading the two bars: below saturation the -5% gap between C_analytic and C_eff is the assumed throughput-efficiency derate; above saturation C_eff - S is unused capacity from insufficient offered demand, not scheduling overhead (demand is capped at 40 rps). Queuing/tail-latency penalties are not determined by this two-line calculation and must be shown separately.' The figure contains three lines (solid C_analytic, dashed C_eff, dotted S) and one shaded region.
issue.acceptance_test: Replace 'the two bars' with 'the two capacity curves' (or 'the three curves'), and make the later reference consistent ('this three-curve construction'). Confirm the caption's description matches the drawn mark types exactly.

issue.issue: The caption presents '21/22-host planning sizing' as the planning answer, but the adjacent text on printed p. 320 states that the fleet must satisfy four requirements — 21, 22, 23 and 32 hosts — with 32 the largest. A reader who takes the figure's caption at face value will under-size the fleet.
issue.evidence: Figure 20.1 caption: '...the 21/22-host planning sizing — 21 ideal / 22 at 95% efficiency — a plateau at the workload's demand ceiling'. In-figure annotation: '21 hosts (ideal) / 22 at 95%: served demand plateaus at 40 rps'. The prose immediately preceding the figure (printed p. 320) says: 'The correct statement is: the fleet must satisfy four requirements — 21 hosts under case (i), 22 hosts under case (ii), with the standard p = 0.95 derate applied to the prefill screen ... case (i) rises to [21.8/0.95] = 23 hosts ... and that the 70% SLO is the prefill screen ... case (ii) is [21.8/0.66] = 32 ... all of 19/21/22/23/32 are illustrative planning scenarios'. The figure models only the throughput/KV-residency screen (17 contexts @ 8.6 s per host) and omits the prefill screen that the prose identifies as binding.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption so the figure's scope is explicit, e.g. 'this figure models the throughput/KV-residency screen only (21 hosts ideal, 22 at 95% efficiency); the prefill screen in Sec. 20.24.1 requires 23 hosts (case i) to 32 hosts (case ii) and is the binding requirement'. Confirm no sentence in the caption or the in-figure annotation presents 21/22 as the fleet size.

issue.figure: FIGURE 20.1, vertical reference lines at N = 21 and N = 22
issue.issue: The two vertical dotted reference lines are one host apart on a 0–60 axis, i.e. roughly 5 pt of separation at print size, and are drawn in the same style, so the reader cannot tell which line is 21 and which is 22.
issue.evidence: The annotation '21 hosts (ideal) / 22 at 95%: served demand plateaus at 40 rps' points at two closely spaced vertical dotted lines near x = 21–22. The knee of the dotted 'actually-served demand' curve is at N = 40/(0.95 x 17/8.6) = 21.3, i.e. between the two lines, so neither line coincides with the visible flattening point.
issue.acceptance_test: Label the two lines directly ('N=21' and 'N=22') with leader text placed at different heights, or use distinct line styles (solid vs dashed) for the two references, and add a marker at the actual knee (N = 21.3). Verify the two references are individually identifiable at 100% print size.

issue.figure: FIGURE 20.1, 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label and dotted line styles
issue.issue: The 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label is set directly on the horizontal dotted reference line, and that line shares its dotted style with the 'actually-served demand' curve, so the two are hard to tell apart where they coincide at the plateau.
issue.evidence: The label 'canonical peak = 40 rps' sits on the y = 40 dotted line at the left of the plot; the legend's third entry 'actually-served demand S = min(40, C_eff) (req/s)' is also a dotted blue line, and the two overlap exactly for N > 21.3.
issue.acceptance_test: Offset the 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label above the line (or add a white halo) and give the horizontal reference a distinct style (e.g. dash-dot) from the S curve. Confirm the reader can trace each of the three curves from the legend to the plateau.

issue.issue: The annotation expresses the derate as '(1-5%)', which is not a well-defined multiplicative factor and reads as a subtraction of 5 percentage points rather than a 5% reduction in capacity.
issue.evidence: In-figure text: 'throughput-efficiency derate = (1-5%) -> C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic'. The legend states the same thing correctly as 'C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic (req/s)'.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite as 'throughput-efficiency derate: x0.95 -> C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic' so the annotation and the legend express the factor identically.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (AI Factory lifecycle) vs FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover)
issue.issue: Two different figures in the book carry the identical number 22.1. PDF p.353 (printed 333, chapter 'The AI Factory') is captioned 'FIGURE 22.1: The model-lifecycle layer runs Data -> Train -> Eval -> Canary -> Observe -> Promote -> Serve.' PDF p.361 (printed 341, chapter 'How to Think Like an AI Solution Architect') is captioned 'FIGURE 22.1: Attention vs. projection prefill FLOP crossover.' The surrounding numbering scheme is chapter-scoped and otherwise unique (23.1 on printed 352, 24.1 on printed 364, 24.4.1 on printed 364, 26.1 on printed 383), so one of the two labels is wrong.
issue.evidence: Printed 333: 'FIGURE 22.1: The model-lifecycle layer runs Data -> Train -> Eval -> Canary -> Observe -> Promote -> Serve.' Printed 341: 'FIGURE 22.1: Attention vs. projection prefill FLOP crossover.' Printed 340: 'Note 22.1-1 (Fig 22.1) - crossover derivation' and printed 341 caption 'Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below.' The note number 22.1-1 and the note's own placement inside the 'How to Think' chapter indicate that chapter 22 owns the crossover figure; the AI Factory figure therefore carries a stale/incorrect number.
issue.acceptance_test: Exactly one figure in the book bears the number 22.1. Renumber the AI Factory figure to its correct chapter-scoped number (e.g. 21.x) and update every in-text, caption, note, and cross-reference that points to it; then re-run the figure-number uniqueness and reference-resolution gates over the whole book.

issue.issue: The caption's takeaway contradicts the derivation note printed on the facing page and the figure's own crossover annotations. The caption says the quadratic attention term 'overestimates the parameterized-linear term at ~53.4K context tokens under full-square counting and ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting, so at 128K it is large but not yet dominant.' By the book's own arithmetic, at 128K the quadratic term is ~2.4x the linear term (full-square) and ~1.2x the linear term (causal-triangle), i.e. it is already the LARGER of the two terms and is 54-71% of total prefill FLOPs. 'Not yet dominant' is false under both conventions and directly contradicts the note on the same spread.
issue.evidence: Printed 340: 'at 128K it is ~2.4x the linear term (linear + quadratic, i.e. 1.2x), and total prefill FLOPs at 128K are ~3.4x the 2N_L baseline'. Independent check: ratio = (N/N*)^2 with N* = 106.8K (causal) gives (128/106.8)^2 = 1.44; with N* = 53.4K (full-square) gives (128/53.4)^2 = 5.74. Either way the quadratic term exceeds the linear term at 128K, so the caption's conclusion is wrong.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the takeaway so it states the crossover as an equality point ('the quadratic term equals the parameterized-linear term at ~53.4K under full-square counting and ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting, and exceeds it beyond those lengths') and replace 'not yet dominant' with the book's own computed ratios at 128K (2.4x full-square / 1.2x causal-triangle, i.e. the quadratic term is already the larger term). Verify the revised sentence against Note 22.1-1 so the caption and note state the same numbers.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), left-panel magenta annotation
issue.issue: The in-figure annotation 'full-square quad overestimates ~53.4x' attaches the number 53.4 to the word 'overestimates', which is a category error and invites a false inference: the reader will conclude that the full-square convention overstates the true attention cost by a factor of 53.4. 53.4K is a crossover CONTEXT LENGTH, not an overestimate factor. The book's own note states the actual overstatement factor is exactly 2x (halving the attention term for the causal mask doubles the crossing).
issue.evidence: Printed 361, left panel: 'full-square quad overestimates ~53.4x'. Printed 340: 'Causal-triangle: halving the attention-part term (see (iii) - a causal mask) doubles the crossing ... so the ~53.4K figure is a property of the full-square convention, and the causal kernel moves it to ~106.8K.' The overstatement factor is 2x; 53.4K is a length on the x-axis.
issue.acceptance_test: Replace the annotation with a statement that names the quantity and the axis, e.g. 'full-square: quadratic = linear at ~53.4K tokens' (and, if the 2x overstatement is worth keeping, state it separately as 'full-square counts 2x the causal attention work'). A reader who has only seen the figure must not be able to conclude that any quantity is overstated by 53.4x.

issue.issue: The derivation note that the figure caption explicitly points to ('Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below') prints a formula that is arithmetically wrong as written: 'L* = N/(n_layers-d) = 70 x (80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens'. The printed expression evaluates to 45,875,200, not 106.8K, and the operator is multiplication where division is required. The correct expression is N* = N_params/(n_layers x d) = 70e9/(80 x 8,192) = 106,811 ~ 106.8K (and 53.4K for the full-square convention, N_params/(2 x n_layers x d)). The two crossover values printed in the figure are correct; the formula that produces them is not.
issue.evidence: Printed 340: 'L* = N/(n_layers-d) = 70 x (80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens'. Recomputation: 70 x 80 x 8,192 = 45,875,200 (not 106.8K). Correct: 70e9 / (80 x 8,192) = 70e9 / 655,360 = 106,811.5 = 106.8K; full-square: 70e9 / (2 x 655,360) = 53,405.8 = 53.4K. Both printed crossover values are reproduced exactly by the corrected formula, confirming the intended derivation.
issue.acceptance_test: Print the derivation as N* = N_params/(n_layers x d) = 70e9/(80 x 8,192) = 106.8K tokens (full-square: N_params/(2 x n_layers x d) = 53.4K), with N_params defined as 70e9 and the units of N* stated as tokens. A reader must be able to reproduce 53.4K and 106.8K by substituting the printed symbols, with no implicit 10^9 and no inverted operator.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), both panels' y-axes
issue.issue: Neither y-axis states a scale factor, so the plotted magnitudes cannot be checked against the stated geometry, and the two panels' vertical positions cannot be reconciled with a single normalization. The left axis is labelled 'Prefill compute (FLOP/request)' but spans 10^-1 to 10^7, which cannot be absolute FLOP/request for the stated 70B model (2 x 70e9 x N is ~1.4e14 at 1K tokens and ~1.4e18 at 10M tokens). The right axis is labelled 'Decode compute (FLOP/token)' with a flat line at ~2e4, whereas 2N for 70B is 1.4e11 FLOP/token. The caption's caveat that 'the panels use different units and are not directly comparable' addresses per-request vs per-token but not the undisclosed scale factors, so a reader comparing the panels' vertical positions will be misled.
issue.evidence: Printed 361: left y-label 'Prefill compute (FLOP/request)', ticks 10^-1..10^7; right y-label 'Decode compute (FLOP/token)', flat line at ~2x10^4; caption 'the panels use different units and are not directly comparable'. Geometry given as '70B, 80-layer, hidden-8,192'. The decode line sits roughly five decades above the prefill linear curve at the left edge of the left panel, whereas per-request vs per-token for this geometry implies about three decades - so a single shared normalization does not explain the drawing.
issue.acceptance_test: State the scale factor on each y-axis (e.g. 'Prefill compute (FLOP/request, x10^15)' and 'Decode compute (FLOP/token, x10^7)') or in the caption, and verify under that factor that (a) the decode line equals 2 x N_params = 1.4e11 FLOP/token, (b) the linear prefill curve equals 2 x N_params x N, and (c) the two panels' vertical offsets are explained by the stated factor difference. If the panels use different factors, say so explicitly.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), x-axis label and marker positions
issue.issue: The x-axis is labelled 'Context length (K tokens)' while the ticks are logarithmic 10^0..10^7. The two readings are not equivalent and the figure's own annotations do not reconcile them: the 'canonical 9.2K' marker is drawn near 10^4 on the axis (which is 9,200 tokens if the ticks are tokens, but 9.2 if the ticks are thousands of tokens), and the crossover annotations '~53.4K' and '~106.8K' are likewise positioned as token counts. As drawn, the axis label and the marker positions disagree, so a reader cannot tell whether the crossover is at 53.4 thousand tokens or at 53.4 million.
issue.evidence: Printed 361: x-axis label 'Context length (K tokens)' on both panels; in-panel text 'canonical 9.2K', 'full-square quad overestimates ~53.4x', 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K'; caption 'at ~53.4K context tokens under full-square counting and ~106.8K under causal-triangle counting'. The 'canonical 9.2K' marker sits near the 10^4 decade, i.e. at 9,200 tokens, not at 9.2.
issue.acceptance_test: Make the axis unit and the marker positions agree: either relabel the axis 'Context length (tokens)' and keep the markers at 9.2e3 / 5.34e4 / 1.068e5, or keep '(K tokens)' and move the markers to 9.2 / 53.4 / 106.8 on the log axis. Verify by reading the marker positions off the rendered axis after the change.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), left panel curve intersections
issue.issue: The two annotated 'crossovers' are not both visible as crossings of the drawn curves, and the caption does not say which intersection each annotation denotes. The magenta 'quadratic' curve is the full-square attention term and the red 'linear' curve is the parameterized-linear term, so their intersection at ~53.4K is the full-square crossover. The green curve is a TOTAL (linear + causal-triangle attention) and therefore never crosses the red linear curve; the causal-triangle crossover at ~106.8K is instead visible as the green/magenta intersection (where linear + causal = full-square, i.e. linear = causal). A reader looking for 'where the green curve meets the red curve' will find no such crossing, and the leader line for the green annotation is not labelled as pointing at the green/magenta intersection.
issue.evidence: Legend on printed 361: 'linear 2-N-L', 'quadratic ...', 'total (full-square)', 'total (causal-triangle)'. Green annotation 'causal-triangle: crossover ~106.8K' with a leader line; magenta annotation 'full-square quad overestimates ~53.4x' with a leader line. Printed 340 note: 'the crossover marked on the left panel ... Causal-triangle: halving the attention-part term ... doubles the crossing'.
issue.acceptance_test: Confirm on the rendered figure that (a) the magenta leader lands on the magenta/red intersection at ~53.4K, (b) the green leader lands on the green/magenta intersection at ~106.8K, and (c) the vertical ordering at the right edge is orange (total full-square) >= magenta (quadratic) >= green (total causal) >= red (linear). Add a one-line caption clause naming the two intersections explicitly, e.g. 'magenta crosses red at ~53.4K; green crosses magenta at ~106.8K'.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover), caption pointer to Note 22.1-1
issue.issue: The caption ends with 'Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below', but Note 22.1-1 is printed on the PRECEDING page (printed 340), above the figure. The pointer sends the reader the wrong way and, combined with the duplicate figure number, makes it easy to land on the wrong note.
issue.evidence: Printed 341 caption: 'Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below.' The note 'Note 22.1-1 (Fig 22.1) - crossover derivation, both FLOP-counting conventions' appears at the top of printed 340, i.e. before the figure.
issue.acceptance_test: Change the pointer to 'Derivation: Note 22.1-1 (previous page)' or move the note below the figure; after the change, verify on the rendered pages that the referenced note is in the stated direction.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (AI Factory lifecycle), FAIL row and rollback band
issue.issue: The red rollback band spans the entire gate row, including the pre-production gates (Data, Train, Eval), and the caption says 'each labelled FAIL branch restores last-known-good state and re-validates'. 'Rollback to last-known-good' is meaningless for a Data/Train/Eval gate failure, where no last-known-good is deployed and the correct action is to fix the pipeline, not to roll back. The figure therefore encodes an operationally wrong recovery semantics for three of its six gates, and the band appears to extend beneath the hatched Serve box, which the caption says is not gated ('Six-box FAIL decision').
issue.evidence: Printed 333 figure: a single solid red band labelled 'rollback to last-known-good & re-validate' drawn under all six gate columns, with six 'FAIL' labels above it; the band appears to run to the right edge under the hatched 'Serve' box. Caption: 'Six-box FAIL decision on a measured metric, not a hand-off. PASS permits the next stage; each labelled FAIL branch restores last-known-good state and re-validates.'
issue.acceptance_test: Restrict the rollback band to the gates that have a deployed predecessor (Canary, Observe, Promote) and label the pre-production gates' failure action differently (e.g. 'fix and re-run'); confirm the band terminates under the Promote column and does not extend beneath the hatched Serve box. The caption must then describe the two distinct failure actions.

issue.issue: The figure's central causal claim - that the Consequences of ADR-001 become the Context of ADR-002 - is asserted by a text label rather than shown by the drawing. The dashed red connector runs from the ADR-001 horizontal rule down to the ADR-002 horizontal rule in the empty space to the right of the field stack; it does not touch the ADR-001 'Consequences' box or the ADR-002 'Context' box. A reader who scans the boxes (the natural reading order) sees two identical five-field stacks and no visual indication of which field feeds which.
issue.evidence: Printed 374 figure: dashed red vertical arrow between the two horizontal rules, with the label 'consequences of ADR-001 become the context of ADR-002' placed to its right; the five field boxes ('Title & status', 'Context', 'Decision', 'Consequences', 'Alternatives') are stacked at the left of both records. Caption: 'The Consequences of ADR-001 become the Context of ADR-002, which supersedes it while the original stays on file.'
issue.acceptance_test: Draw the connector from the ADR-001 'Consequences' box to the ADR-002 'Context' box (a routed elbow that visibly terminates on both boxes), or add explicit field-level markers (e.g. a 'becomes' tag on the ADR-001 Consequences box and a 'from ADR-001' tag on the ADR-002 Context box). Verify on the rendered page that the connector's endpoints touch the two named boxes.

issue.figure: Table 22.1 (continuation), 'KV cache memory per request' row
issue.issue: The derivation cell reads '2.62 MB/token x 9,200 / 9,500 tokens', where the slash is ambiguous between 'or' and division; read literally it is a division. The same cell is set in a column so narrow that it wraps to roughly one or two words per line over ~18 lines, which is both a legibility problem and a sign that the table's column widths are misallocated (the value column is nearly empty while the derivation column is starved). The arithmetic itself is correct.
issue.evidence: Printed 340: value '~24.1 GB (8xK, FP16) / ~24.9 GB (9.5K max)'; derivation '2.62 MB/token x 9,200 / 9,500 tokens [ILLUSTRATIVE] [DERIVED]'. Check: 2.62 MB x 9,200 = 24,104 MB = 24.1 GB; 2.62 MB x 9,500 = 24,890 MB = 24.9 GB - both correct.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the derivation as '2.62 MB/token x 9,200 tokens = 24.1 GB; x 9,500 tokens = 24.9 GB' (or 'x 9,200 (or 9,500) tokens'), and rebalance the column widths so no cell wraps below roughly six words per line. Confirm the rendered table has no line of fewer than four words.

issue.figure: FIGURE 22.1 (AI Factory lifecycle), green feedback arrow

issue.issue: The 'Serve' box is drawn with a diagonal hatch while every other stage is solid, but neither the figure nor the caption explains what the hatch encodes. The reader can infer 'not gated' from the caption's 'Six-box FAIL decision', but the encoding is left to inference, and in grayscale the hatch is the only thing distinguishing Serve from the other stages.

issue.issue: The legend entry for the quadratic curve is not a legible formula at print size; it renders as something like 'quadratic 4_n layers L^2-d', which does not state the quantity being plotted (the full-square attention term 4 x n_layers x d^2 x N^2). issue.figure: FIGURE 23.1 (From vague ask to architectural bounds), caption

KV precision FP16->FP8 + prefix cache + routing'.

issue.issue: The six stage boxes are distinguished only by hue (dark red, red, orange, purple, teal, blue). In grayscale, boxes 2, 4, 5 and 6 collapse to similar mid-tones, and the red feedback loop becomes a mid-gray line of similar weight to the black forward-flow arrows. The figure survives only because each box carries a number and a label; the color carries no redundant information. This is a weaker encoding discipline than the one used elsewhere in the book (FIGURE 26.1 uses hatch patterns as well as color).

issue.acceptance_test: Add a redundant non-color encoding to the six stage boxes (e.g. distinct hatch density, or a shape/weight difference), or confirm on a grayscale print proof that the numbered labels alone are sufficient and that the feedback loop remains distinguishable from the forward arrows by routing and weight.

issue.issue: The composition is left-heavy: the five-field stacks occupy a narrow column at the left while roughly the right half of the figure area is empty except for the two centered record titles and one italic annotation. issue.acceptance_test: Either move 'kept, not edited' adjacent to the 'ADR-001 (superseded)' title (or into the ADR-001 rule line) so its referent is unambiguous, or rebalance the layout so the right-hand whitespace is reduced and the two records read as a single column of content.

issue.figure: FIGURE 26.1 (Workload fingerprints on the six axes)

'Six axes' implies a six-dimensional space (which is what the parenthetical 'grouped bars, not radar' is implicitly disclaiming), and the prose on the facing page repeats the phrase: 'the six axes (context length, traffic, quality required, cost sensitivity, latency sensitivity, output tokens)'. 'Six dimensions' or 'six workload characteristics' would be exact.

Printed 383 prose: 'the six axes (context length, traffic, quality required, cost sensitivity, latency sensitivity, output tokens) are subjective normalized scores (0-1)'.
